entries.title: Two other apps on the same origin delete Freelief's offline cache, and Freelief then fails to open offline until its next version
Boot has no failure path: one failed start-up fetch or module leaves a blank page with no breathing guide and no 'Need urgent help?' control
Any push to main is a public deploy, but the rules call a phone-test push 'not a release', so the audit gate never applies to what users get, and v0.5.0 is live without a round
Freelief shares its web origin with three other sites, and any of them can rewrite its offline cache and settings
The router accepts inherited object names from the URL hash, so a link such as #constructor gives a blank app and a stuck router
The Feedback page does not tell the person that a GitHub issue is public
The design's control against a tampered crisis line ('every change goes through a reviewed commit') is not in place
A failed data load on a deep link to Standards stops the router, and from another screen it leaves a frozen copy of the previous screen
The update test that the design names as the mitigation for a stale offline cache does not exist
Nothing checks that a change to a shipped file comes with a version bump, so installed users can keep an old file, including a changed crisis line, indefinitely
test and build check the working tree, not the commit that GitHub Pages deploys
The browser that the tests, bench and icon tool need is not installed by setup, not checked by doctor and not declared
The worker's precache fills a new versioned cache through the browser HTTP cache, so a new version can freeze old files
Freelief's activate deletes every cache on the shared origin, not only its own
The colour sort shipped under a rule that dropped the manual accessibility check that RLG-005 requires
REQ-014 carries status 'agreed' although the implementer rewrote its text and the owner has not agreed to it
RLG-001 is marked built while its own done-when (the owner's phone check) is still open, no owner check for any slice is recorded, and slices 2 to 5 were built on top of it
The colour sort is missing from the Standards and research page and sources.md, and nothing maps an activity to a technique
The emergency number in the urgent-help dialog is plain text, not a tap-to-call link
REQ-030 (must) requires the email route, but the design allows a release with the email button hidden
The project's audit pace was not followed: no round ran at the end of slices 1 to 4
The declared ROUTING_BIAS 2 is not in force: every unit ran at bias 1
A recorded standard has no version, so a claim outlives the version it was checked for
The success criterion that crisis-line dates are no older than the release has no check and no release date to check against
The claim 'sends nothing after install' omits the browser's update check to GitHub on each online launch
A device with no region set is shown the lines and emergency number of a guessed country, not the unknown-region path
The offline test and the network test cover only breathing and the help dialog, not every screen
No supported-browser baseline is stated, and the suite runs only in Chromium for a phone-first app
`run` serves the whole repository, including .git, .venv and input/excluded, on all network interfaces
The stored-settings check accepts inherited object names, so a stored rhythm of 'constructor' breaks the breathing guide
No test guards the CSP, and the static external-load check misses common forms
setup installs the test dependencies unpinned and with no lock file
Pages build HTML from data with escaping that is not consistent
doctor reports the tests collectable after only counting files, and AGENTS.md repeats the claim
doctor silently skips a JSON file that is missing
doctor does not check the service worker or two of the shipped JSON files, though the design says it does
bench fails with a raw traceback when the .venv is missing
The breathing guide and the bubble field keep every timer id for the whole session
User-facing text outside the strings file breaks REQ-017
The public README still describes two distraction activities; the colour sort is not named
Design Stage 8 disagrees with the code on the ctx contract, the tunables, the routes and inline CSS
AGENTS.md Architecture lists only the menu and Settings as screens
The tagline 'Breathe with the circle' shows on every screen, including screens with no circle
The urgent-help dialog can be closed by touch only from its bottom, after all the content
The design document has a literal '\n' in the Decision Log and a stale Document Control
The reduced-motion guide scale is an in-code constant, not a config.json tunable
motion.onMotionChange is exported but nothing calls it
No record shows the look variants that the design says the implementer shows the owner
Saved 'tones on' plays nothing at launch until the person taps, and nothing says so
Forced-colors (high contrast) mode is not handled, so the colour-sort tiles can look the same
The design does not say what happens when the phone screen sleeps during breathing
The 'Chat online' crisis link does not say that it needs a network
No stated handling exists for a feedback issue from a person who is in danger
No procedure turns a volunteer accessibility check into a recorded standard
The Feedback page puts the person's whole message into the GitHub link's URL, so the text reaches browser history and GitHub when the link opens, before the person submits anything
'Update now' deletes the offline copy and the worker before it knows the network works, so on a dead or captive connection the app is gone until the device is online again
After a touch, a mid-session update serves the new version's lazy screens to the old shell, and a screen that cannot load bounces to the menu and leaves its own link dead
bench enforces only the hard targets, not the recorded tolerance, and launch and size are each 34% over baseline with no log entry since v0.5.10
The worker's fetch handler has no catch, so a Cache Storage error answers every request with a network error, even online
The worker reports whether the cache repair worked, but nothing listens, so a failed repair is invisible

The trust page and the default-rhythm decision say that a longer out-breath did better than box breathing in Balban 2023, but the trial did not test that comparison, and 4-in 6-out was not one of its arms
Settings saves every default as if the person chose it, so the new long out-breath default never reaches anyone who changed any setting while box breathing was the default

docs/research/sources.md, the written research record, is out of step with data/research.json: it lacks eight cited sources and their evidence notes, keeps removed techniques, and now makes a false statement about the colour sort
The owner's decision to open on the menu was never carried into AGENTS.md, Design F1, Stages 2, 6 and 8, or the README, which still say that the breathing guide starts at launch

The design keeps superseded figures and rules after the owner's changes, so the 1.0 release criteria require a 150 KB size that REQ-028 replaced, and F2, the risk table, Settings, deploy and requirement-range clauses are stale
The Visualizer activity reads and writes Settings itself, which breaks the boundary that activities stay free of storage
About's privacy text and the design's definition of Settings list three stored items, but Freelief stores six, including the chosen region
The Delivery Plan ends at slice 5, so 31 versions of new features belong to no slice, and the slice-end audit pace and the minor bump never fire
The Visualizer, the vibration module and the start-up fallback have no place in the design's vocabulary, flows or module table, or in AGENTS.md Architecture
The accessibility-check checklist names a 'More ways to calm' screen that no longer exists and lists none of the activities, and nav.settingsHint outlived the menu change unused
The thread's next action points at work that is already built
Each commit carries a store index that lags its own fragments: at HEAD it shows UNT-050 open and RLG-025 requested, and it omits UNT-051
The live preview was moved about nine times after v0.5.2 with no record of the owner's yes or of which version is live
Nothing stops or quiets sound when urgent help opens or when the person leaves the app to call a line
Visualizer full screen and black screen hide 'Need urgent help?', and the design states no exception to 'every screen'

the project clear tally
Freelief offers a paced breathing exercise with a visual breath guide.
Freelief offers a 5-4-3-2-1 sensory grounding exercise that the person steps through at their own pace.
Freelief offers calming statements, shown one at a time, that the person advances at their own pace.
Freelief offers interactive calming activities whose purpose is to distract the person from panic.

Every screen shows a 'Need urgent help?' control that opens the crisis lines of one region, chosen from a region saved in Settings or else from the device language and region setting, with a country list to show another region, without a request for location.
The main screen shows one short line that says Freelief is self-help and not medical care, and the About page gives the full statement. Neither blocks access to an exercise.

Freelief plays subtle sounds: a soft tone that lasts each breathing phase, and short cues for the activities (a bubble pop, a singing-glass tone while tracing, a click and a rising phrase in the colour sort). Sounds are on by default; the speaker button in the header turns them all off at once. Nothing plays before the person's first tap or key press.
Freelief is a progressive web app served from GitHub Pages that installs to the home screen and works with no network after the first visit.
Every control is reachable and usable with a keyboard alone and with a screen reader.
When the device asks for reduced motion, Freelief replaces every animation with a still or gentle equivalent.
No exercise or activity requires the person to act within a time limit.
Freelief offers a bubble field: the person pops slow, soft bubbles by touch or by key, with no score, no failure and no timer.
Freelief offers a shape trace: the person slowly follows a looping shape with a finger or the arrow keys.

Freelief offers a colour sort: the person puts calm colours into order from lightest to darkest by choosing a tile and then the tile to swap it with, by touch, mouse or keyboard, or by dragging a tile onto another tile by touch or mouse, with no score and no failure.
Freelief collects no personal data and sends nothing over the network after install. Only the person's settings are stored, and only on the device.
Freelief meets WCAG 2.2 level AA in full, and level AAA wherever a criterion can be met.
All user-facing text lives in one strings file per language, so a translation can be added without a code change. English is the only language in the first version.

When Freelief opens, it shows the menu of exercises and activities at once, with no account, sign-up, notice or question before it; the person can choose in Settings to open on breathing instead. Breathing is the first item, one tap away, and every screen has a Back to menu control.
Freelief is plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no framework, no third-party dependency and no build step.

A "Standards & research" page, linked from the footer and the disclaimer page, promotes every standard Freelief meets, such as WCAG 2.2 AA, with its level and the date it was last verified. It lists only standards that a check has verified.
Freelief uses a dark, calm theme by default and follows the device light or dark setting. All text meets WCAG AAA contrast (7:1, or 4.5:1 for large text).
Freelief ships a curated list of national crisis lines, each with a last-checked date, and a link to an international directory for every other region.
The person can choose a breathing rhythm from presets (4-in 6-out by default, a slower rhythm, and box breathing), and the choice is remembered on the device.
Every technique in Freelief is one studied in published clinical research, and the Standards & research page cites at least one source for each technique.

Freelief makes no claim that it is clinically proven, treats, cures or diagnoses anything. It may say only that its techniques are studied in clinical research, and may claim a review or certification only after it is granted.
On a mid-range phone, installed and offline, the first screen (the menu) is visible within 1 second of a cold launch.
Every tap or key press gets a visible response within 100 milliseconds on a mid-range phone.
The whole app, with every file the offline cache stores, is under 250 KB.

A standard is shown as met only when an automated check of every page passes and a manual check with a screen reader and with a keyboard alone is recorded, with its date and tester, for the version shown. The manual check may come from community volunteers.

A feedback page opens a pre-filled GitHub issue (accessibility check or problem report) and, as a second choice, a pre-filled email to the public project address. The pre-filled text holds only the app version, browser and device type, and the person sees and can edit all of it before they send. The app itself sends nothing.
Freelief's source code is published under the MIT license.
Freelief offers a ripple pond: the person touches still water, or presses a key, and soft ripples spread from that point, by touch, mouse or keyboard, with no score and no failure.

Freelief offers mandala coloring: the person chooses a soft color and taps or selects a part of a mandala to fill it, by touch, mouse or keyboard, with every part named for a screen reader, and with no score and no failure.

Freelief gives a short vibration on a single triggered event in an activity (a pop, a choice, a swap, a finished sort, a finished loop, a ripple, a fill), never for anything continuous, where the device supports it; a Settings switch turns it off, and it is on by default.
